items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Terminology 46:1
items.html: Illuminations whose way is to be extinguished, and which are destined to be awakened and to kindle and to shine again as at first, are called “sparks.” For they resemble the sparks that remain after a fire, or those that fly out from under the hammer in a craftsman’s hand: although they appear to be going out, they are nevertheless liable to kindle into a great and terrible flame. And the said illuminations do not occur except in reflected light. (Part 4, Chapter 3, Item 10)
